CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for her annual exam. It has been one year since her last visit.

Rheumatoid Arthritis: Patient reports compliance with recommended exercise regimen including walking, yoga, and exercise. She notes these activities have significantly helped with her arthritis. Denies any joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups over the past year. Currently taking methotrexate once weekly with no issues tolerated.

Atrial Fibrillation: Patient continues to experience palpitations. Last episode was approximately one week ago. She has noticed palpitations tend to flare up with stress. She has tried meditation and running with her dog to manage stress but reports limited benefit. An event monitor was performed last month.

Reflux: Patient has made dietary modifications including eliminating soda, which has helped. She reports medication has also been helpful. Denies flare-ups for over five months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses palpitations and nasal congestion related to allergies. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
Atrial fibrillation
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
Protonix

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Heart rate well-controlled
Heart: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, regular rate and rhythm
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Right elbow: Edema and erythema noted with pain to palpation
Lower extremities: No edema

RESULTS
Event monitor: Shows patient transitioning in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses. Patient enters atrial fibrillation, pauses, then returns to regular rhythm.
Autoimmune panel: All values normal. Rheumatoid arthritis well controlled on current methotrexate therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Rheumatologist referral available if needed. Disease appears stable. Methotrexate refilled.

2. Atrial fibrillation: Patient experiencing intermittent episodes. Referral to cardiology for cardiac ablation procedure to map and ablate the source of the rhythm abnormality with goal of maintaining normal sinus rhythm. Patient counseled that she is young and should be kept in normal rhythm.

3. Reflux: Continue protonix 40 mg daily. Continue dietary modifications including avoiding coffee and spicy foods. Patient to report any additional concerns.
